Laredo College has given a permanent home to the memory of one of its own transformational leaders. The college dedicated a memorial bench and magnolia tree honoring the late Carolyn M. Schmies, placing the bench alongside that of her beloved daughter Cesha Monique Brown, so both can “continue to watch over new generations of students,” according to Laredo College.

Schmies’ husband, Kenneth R. Schmies, a member of the Laredo College Education Foundation, used the moment to announce a $500 annual scholarship that will support a student with special needs in pursuing their academic goals.

“Carolyn was a dear friend and a cherished member of the Palomino family. She was a source of light, love and encouragement to everyone around her,” Laredo College President Dr. Minita Ramírez said, according to the college.

Schmies’ career was defined by firsts. A former Indianapolis sixth-grade teacher, she moved into General Motors, where she became the first female and African-American supervisor in the company and was later promoted to its first female buyer, according to the college. She went on to leadership roles across the U.S. and Mexico with GM/Delphi before arriving at Laredo College.

She started at the South Campus as an adjunct speech instructor and within a year was promoted to chair of the Reading and Communication Department. In 2019 she was named Interim South Campus Dean and was shortly afterward officially named Dean of the South Campus. She retired in 2021 after 12 years of service but continued charitable work in retirement.

Her civic footprint was just as wide: president of United Way of Laredo, president of Literacy Volunteers of Laredo, vice president of the Optimist Club, and a Leadership Women regional ambassador, among other roles.

The magnolia tree, donated by Leadership Women, will grow and provide shade for generations of students. “Lifelong learning was certainly something that Carolyn was known for. She was an educator at heart,” said Leadership Women Chief Operating Officer Heidi K. Murray, according to the college.
